rfm_tuples.R: Net income (loss) $728,642 [thousand] ... improved from a net income of $364.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2022 to $728.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify GAAP net income via consolidated statement of operations; cross-check Adjusted Net Income reconciliation; verify Q1-2024 follow-through via 10-Q (Mode B: did profitability persist into the quarter post-cutoff-prior?).
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY23 GAAP NI $728.6M confirmed. FY23 Adjusted NI $501M (vs $474M FY22). However, Q1-2024 swung to a net loss of $(3.75)M vs $237.9M in Q1-2023 — a >$240M YoY swing driven by crack-spread compression ($131.8M decrease in legacy refining margins).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 10-K headline number is honest, but the Q1 follow-up reveals the FY23 profit pulse has already broken. Disclosure is accurate; underlying refining cycle has clearly rolled over. Not a lying signal; a cyclical signal.

rfm_tuples.R: Deloitte & Touche LLP ... We have served as the Company's auditor since 2013. ... [no going-concern paragraph; clean unqualified audit opinion with Billings purchase-price-allocation noted as Critical Audit Matter].
rfm_tuples.f: Verify auditor identity and tenure; verify no going-concern or substantial-doubt language anywhere in the audit opinion or footnotes; verify CAM disclosure is non-distressed in nature (Mode A + B).
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 8 — Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm; full-text search of 10-K for 'going concern', 'substantial doubt'
rfm_tuples.M_value: Big-4 auditor (Deloitte) since 2013, no change. Zero hits on 'going concern' or 'substantial doubt'. CAM is purchase-price allocation for Billings Acquisition (valuation complexity), not impairment or recoverability. Annual-meeting proxy (8-K 2024-05-02) reaffirmed Deloitte for FY24.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No audit-side distress signal. The single CAM is a routine acquisition-accounting matter, not a liquidity or going-concern flag.

rfm_tuples.R: On August 2, 2023, the Board expanded the Company's share repurchase program from $50 million to $250 million. ... For the three months ended March 31, 2024, 906 thousand shares were repurchased under this share repurchase program for $32 [million] ... $159.4 million of authorization remaining.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify capital-return behavior is consistent with insider confidence; verify pace of repurchases against cash-flow capacity and debt covenants (Mode B: a distressed company should not be returning capital).
rfm_tuples.M_value: $32M of Q1-2024 repurchases (~906k shares, implied ~$35/share) executed AFTER drawdown began. Board expanded program 5x in Aug-2023. No covenant blocks on repurchases. Cash balance $228M at 3/31/24.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strong Mode-A pass: management is actively buying back stock during the drawdown — the opposite of what distressed managements do. This is a LONG-tier confidence signal.

rfm_tuples.R: On February 28, 2023 ... entered into the Term Loan Credit Agreement ... due 2030 ... 7.75% Senior Secured Notes due 2025 ... we repurchased and cancelled $260 [million] in aggregate principal ... at 102.120%. ... Subsequent Events: On April 8, 2024, the Term Loan Credit Agreement was amended ... reduction in the Applicable Margin under the Term Loan Credit Agreement by 50 basis points ...
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the direction of capital-structure amendments — distressed names get covenant relief and HIGHER spreads; healthy names get spread REDUCTIONS (Mode B: April-2024 amendment is the smoking gun for which way the market views PARR's credit).
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note on long-term debt + 10-Q Note 20 Subsequent Events + 8-K filed 2024-04-09 (0001437749-24-011487)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Term Loan Credit Agreement matures Feb-2030 (refinanced FY23 from 2026). April-2024 amendment REDUCED applicable margin by 50bps (lenders cutting price). Also Mar-22-2024 Third ABL Amendment increased total revolver commitment to $1.4B and added PHR as borrower in preparation for J. Aron termination.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Banks are cutting spreads and EXPANDING commitments — the polar opposite of distress. This is a strong LONG-tier counter-indicator vs the drawdown.

rfm_tuples.R: We have a supply and offtake agreement with J. Aron ... the Supply and Offtake Agreement expires May 31, 2024 (as extended, the 'Expiration Date'). ... Upon termination of the Supply and Offtake Agreement ... we are obligated to repurchase all crude oil and refined product inventories then owned by J. Aron ... This repurchase obligation could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, or financial condition.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: A risk factor names a hard expiration 16 days after cutoff, with potential MAE if not refinanced. Verify a replacement facility is being lined up; quantify the obligation; verify funding source.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Risk Factors + 10-Q Note 8 + 8-K filed 2024-03-27 (Third ABL Amendment)
rfm_tuples.M_value: S&O obligations at 3/31/24 = $662.7M (vs $594.4M at 12/31/23). Mar-22-2024 Third ABL Amendment increased revolver to $1.4B SPECIFICALLY 'to permit a new intermediation facility in favor of PHR' subject to termination of the existing J. Aron arrangement. Sequencing is clean — refinancing already executed before cutoff. Pattern matches the Washington Refinery Intermediation Agreement wind-down (terminated Q4-2023 via Second ABL Amendment).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Material risk factor is mitigated by a fully-disclosed pre-cutoff refinancing path. Mode-B follow-through verified. The disclosure is honest and forward-looking; the company solved the problem before the calendar deadline.

rfm_tuples.R: We sell a variety of refined products to a diverse customer base. ... For each of the years ended December 31, 2023, 2022, and 2021, we had one customer in our refining segment that accounted for 13%, 17%, and 13%, respectively, of our consolidated revenue. No other customer accounted for more than 10%.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: 13%-of-revenue single counterparty is material but UNNAMED. Verify whether the customer can be identified from segment disclosures or 8-Ks; assess concentration trend.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Customer is not named. Concentration moved 13% → 17% → 13% over 2021-2023 — not increasing structurally. Likely a wholesale-distribution / military / utility counterparty given Hawaii market structure, but PARR refuses to disclose identity. Per the entity-resolution rule, the counterparty mirror via edgar_fts is not feasible without a name.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B finding: PARR could have named the customer (most refiners do via Hawaiian Electric / DLA Energy / specific airline disclosures) and chose not to. Modest opacity, but disclosed magnitude is small and trend is flat-to-down.

rfm_tuples.R: Critical Audit Matter Description: On June 1, 2023, the Company completed the acquisition ... for a total purchase price of $625.4 million ... Billings Acquisition Valuation and Purchase Price Allocation.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A + B: verify the acquisition price, funding source, and whether the PPA is producing impairment risk; check for any change-in-segment, goodwill, or earnout disclosures.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 5 (Acquisitions) + CAM disclosure + Term Loan refinancing context
rfm_tuples.M_value: $625.4M Billings Acquisition closed 6/1/2023, funded by refinanced Term Loan (Feb-2023 $260M repurchase of 7.75% notes + new Term Loan due 2030). PPA still in measurement period at 12/31/23 — CAM language flags this as 'challenging, subjective, or complex'. No goodwill impairment trigger noted. 65% / 40% equity interests in YELP / YPLC consolidated/equity-method.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Billings is a large-relative-to-equity acquisition (purchase price ~50% of pre-deal equity). PPA is mid-process and could produce step-ups/impairments in future quarters. Worth flagging but not a 'lying' signal — the auditor flagged it openly via CAM.

rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2023, we owned a 46% equity investment in Laramie Energy, LLC ... the book value of such investment had been reduced to zero ... we suspended the application of the equity method of accounting for our investment in Laramie Energy ...
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: a previously-impaired equity investment that's been zeroed could surface upside via natgas-price recovery; verify whether PARR has guaranteed any Laramie debt or has recourse exposure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Laramie carried at $0 ($14.3M residual disclosed but book value 0 for equity-method purposes). PARR explicitly does not control Laramie. No PARR guarantees on Laramie debt disclosed. Suspension of equity method is a conservative accounting posture, not a write-down event.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Old wound, properly disclosed and walled off. Optionality (free upside) exists if natgas rallies. No hidden recourse.

rfm_tuples.R: During the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2023, no director or officer (as defined in Rule 16a-1(f) of the Securities Exchange Act) of the Company adopted [10b5-1 trading arrangements].
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify no insider Rule 10b5-1 plan adoption. Mode B: cross-check with Section 16 filings via EDGAR for actual insider transactions during the drawdown window (Sep 2023 - May 2024).
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9B + EDGAR Form 4 search (not pulled in this pilot, but the absence-of-disclosure is itself the M-value)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Officers/directors did NOT pre-arrange selling plans in Q4-2023 (the quarter when the drawdown was accelerating). This means any insider sales would have to be on open-window, full-disclosure basis. No 8-K announcements of insider sales were filed in the pre-cutoff window I reviewed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No defensive 10b5-1 plan adoption during the drawdown — insiders did not lock in selling. Combined with $32M of company repurchases, this is a coherent 'we believe stock is cheap' signal.

rfm_tuples.R: Refined product crack spreads in the first quarter of 2024 decreased as compared to the first quarter of 2023. ... 3-1-2 Singapore Crack Spread ... $131.8 million related to decreased crack spreads at our refineries in our legacy portfolio.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: 13% net-loss swing in Q1 absent any company-specific bad news = pure crack-spread cyclicality. Verify by cross-checking that the FY23 high earnings power was crack-spread-driven and is mean-reverting, not structurally broken.
rfm_tuples.M_value: PARR explicitly attributes the Q1 swing to (a) crack-spread compression $131.8M, (b) higher environmental (RINs) costs $125M, (c) inventory-financing rate increases, partially offset by Billings contribution. No refinery shutdowns, accidents, force-majeure, or covenant trips. Throughput 181 Mbpd healthy. Annualized sensitivity: $1/bbl crack-spread move = $65M op-income.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Drawdown is fully explained by sector-wide crack-spread normalization off 2022-2023 highs — not by company-specific deterioration. This is honestly disclosed cyclicality, not concealed distress.

summary: PARR is a Deloitte-audited Big-4 refiner with no going-concern language, no material weakness, no restatement, no covenant trips, and $228M cash. The 30.8% drawdown is fully explained by crack-spread normalization off the 2022-23 highs (FY23 NI $728.6M -> Q1-24 NI $(3.75)M, attributed by PARR to $131.8M crack-spread compression and $125M RINs cost). The credit market is signaling the OPPOSITE of distress: in the 8 weeks BEFORE cutoff, lenders (i) expanded the ABL revolver to $1.4B and (ii) cut the Term Loan applicable margin by 50bps. Management bought back $32M of stock in Q1-24 during the drawdown and had not pre-arranged any 10b5-1 plans in Q4-23. The J. Aron supply-and-offtake expiry (May 31, 2024) was already mitigated pre-cutoff via the Third ABL Amendment. Honestly-disclosed cyclical pain at a structurally sound company. Per the honesty-alpha framework, the framework's job is to EXCLUDE this name from the SHORT bucket, not to short it.
